_comment: Two B-roll clips for the INTRO of the Bhag Singh reel. The user's rule: in the upper half only the court photograph and the judges' portraits may be stills — everything else must be Flow animation matched to what is being narrated. These replace the static LAWWORLD card (0-6.3s, while he introduces himself and the channel) and the static headline card (12.95-17.5s, while he names Section 100 and hands off to the story). Run with --broll: no avatar, no dialogue, so Flow is never asked to name a judge or report news, both of which it refuses.
brollSetting: Set in Indian legal surroundings: an advocate's chambers, law reports, case files and land records. Warm, authoritative, documentary realism. Any people are Indian and in ordinary professional clothing.

globalStyle.negativePrompts: NO readable text, NO letters or numbers on screen, NO book titles, NO signage with words, NO logos, NO watermarks; NO recognisable real person, NO judge, NO politician; NO judge presiding in a courtroom; NO cartoon, NO illustration, NO 3D render
globalStyle.camera: Cinematic vertical 9:16, 35mm lens look, shallow depth of field, smooth slow camera movement, eye level
globalStyle.realism: Photorealistic live-action documentary footage, warm motivated light, natural texture, fine film grain, rich filmic colour grade

scenes.brollRealistic: A traditional Indian advocate's chambers at golden hour: tall wooden shelves packed with worn red and maroon bound law reports, a heavy desk in the foreground with neat stacks of case files tied in red string, a brass desk lamp lit, warm light falling through a tall window with slow dust in the air; slow drift forward between the shelves, nobody in frame.

Close on a pair of hands untying the red cloth binding of an old bundle of land records on a dark wooden desk and folding the cloth back to reveal layered yellowed papers; a brass lamp throws warm light across them; very slow push in, shallow focus on the topmost sheet.
